cases.scenario: D6 two-layer TC full re-run (imp015_tc.sh): SQL correctness battery (QA1/QB1/QC1/QC2) base-vs-patch EXACT compare + shell arming proof (TA/TB trace, hash mode + parallel workers sub-line) on both variants
cases.expected: layer1 cross-variant EXACT identical + natural==serialref both variants; layer2 base shows NO parallel sub-line (workers=0), patch shows workers>=2 under both hash:partial (TA) and hash:true/spill (TB)
cases.observed: base TA/TB workers=0 (hash_ok=true); patch TA workers=6 under hash:partial, TB workers=6 under hash:true (spill); layer1 compare pass=true for all 4 queries (cross_variant_identical, base_natural_eq_serialref, patch_natural_eq_serialref all true)

cases.expected: 0 rows selected on both variants, byte-identical (also exercises D1(a)'s runtime-state read against a groupby with zero input tuples)
1 row selected, identical aggregates on both variants

cases.scenario: all-NULL GROUP BY key -> single NULL group (t_allnull, 40000 rows, k always NULL)
cases.expected: 1 group (k=NULL), COUNT=40000, identical on both variants; NULL-key handling unaffected by the caller-side runtime-truth formula

cases.scenario: single group, all 40000 rows share one non-NULL key (t_singlegroup)
cases.expected: 1 group, COUNT=40000, identical aggregates on both variants

cases.scenario: mixed NULL/non-NULL keys, high selectivity (t_mixednull: ~1/7 rows NULL, rest near-unique -> ~85.7% distinct, arms HS_REJECT_ALL); adversarial vs D6 TC because the D6 battery never mixes NULL keys into an armed high-selectivity table
cases.expected: 34286 groups (1 NULL group + 34285 distinct), EXACT cross-variant identical results; trace: base workers=0 under hash:partial (D2 gate refuses while HS_REJECT_ALL was not runtime-observable pre-patch), patch workers>=2 under hash:partial (D2(a) fires)
cases.observed: 34286 rows both variants, cross_variant_identical=true; trace base GROUPBY hash:partial workers=0; trace patch GROUPBY hash:partial workers=6

cases.scenario: composite (multi-column) GROUP BY key (k1,k2), high selectivity (t_composite, 40000 rows, 100% distinct (k1,k2)); adversarial vs D6 TC because the D6 battery only exercises single-column keys
cases.expected: 40000 groups, EXACT cross-variant identical (sort key tie-breaking across 2 columns must be stable under a parallel fallback sort too); trace: base workers=0, patch workers>=2 under hash:partial
cases.observed: 40000 rows both variants, cross_variant_identical=true; trace base GROUPBY hash:partial workers=0; trace patch GROUPBY hash:partial workers=6

cases.scenario: HAVING + uncorrelated scalar subquery on an armed GROUP BY (GROUP BY k1 HAVING SUM(v) > (SELECT AVG(v) FROM t_mixednull))
cases.expected: identical filtered row set/values on both variants; HAVING evaluation and the subquery's own (unrelated) groupby state must not interact with the caller-side runtime truth of the outer query's sort
cases.observed: 39622 rows both variants (378 groups filtered out by HAVING), cross_variant_identical=true

cases.scenario: negative control: extreme LOW selectivity, 3 groups over 40000 rows (t_extreme) -- must stay unaffected per spec sec.B item 8 (negative controls)
cases.expected: hash state stays HS_ACCEPT_ALL (never rejects, no spill since only 3 distinct groups), so hash:true with NO parallel sub-line on EITHER variant -- D2(a)'s formula must not spuriously fire when the runtime hash state was never rejected
cases.observed: 3 rows both variants, cross_variant_identical=true; trace BOTH variants show GROUPBY hash:true workers=0 (identical, no parallel sub-line anywhere)

cases.scenario: order-sensitive GROUP_CONCAT(v ORDER BY v) over a 4000-group/40000-row table (t_concat_hs) -- D4 check, extends D6's QC1/QC2 (which use low-cardinality groups) to a table sized/shaped so the fallback sort itself naturally parallelizes
cases.expected: GROUP_CONCAT member order per group is deterministic (explicit inner ORDER BY v) and EXACT cross-variant identical; per D4/A4 the aggregate is not hash-eligible at plan time so IMP-015's caller-side formula for (a) is moot here -- confirmed by trace showing hash:false on BOTH variants, i.e. this path was already outside hash_eligible gating before the patch
cases.observed: 4000 rows both variants, cross_variant_identical=true; trace BOTH variants show GROUPBY hash:false sort:true workers=6 (identical -- the parallel fallback sort for order-sensitive aggregates pre-existed IMP-015 and is unaffected by it, consistent with D4)

cases.scenario: same-session 10x sequential repeat of an armed query (composite-key GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT 500) -- reproducibility/determinism probe for the new parallel fallback sort path
cases.expected: all 10 in-session repeats produce byte-identical result sets on each variant (parallel workers introduce no run-to-run nondeterminism)
cases.observed: base: 10/10 runs identical (1 distinct hash); patch: 10/10 runs identical (1 distinct hash) -- confirmed AFTER fixing a harness canonicalization bug (per-statement 'in Line N>' trace-block header text varies by script position and was initially miscounted as a real diff; fixed by stripping it before hashing, then reverified both variants pass with genuinely identical row data)

cases.scenario: 4-session concurrency stress: 4 concurrent csql sessions x 3 iterations each of the same armed composite-key GROUP BY query, against the patched (and, as a control, base) engine -- latch/deadlock/crash probe for the newly-parallel fallback sort under concurrent load
cases.expected: no ERROR in any session's stdout/stderr, no nonzero csql exit code, and all 12 result sets per variant are byte-identical to each other (no cross-session interference/corruption)
cases.observed: base: 4 sessions x 3 iters = 12/12 results identical, 0 errors; patch: 4 sessions x 3 iters = 12/12 results identical, 0 errors -- no latch contention, deadlock, or crash observed under concurrent parallel-sort load

cases.scenario: campaign DB (tpch_sf10_q1, read-only) Q10 run on the real IMP-015 binary, SET TRACE ON, checking the parallel-workers sub-line under the outer GROUPBY (spec sec.C criterion 1)

cases.scenario: campaign DB (tpch_sf10_q1, read-only) Q18 run on the real IMP-015 binary, SET TRACE ON, checking for a parallel-workers sub-line on the l_orderkey HAVING-subquery's GROUPBY (spec sec.B item 5/7: upper-bound observation only, not a gate)
cases.expected: query completes and returns 100 rows; observational only -- no pass/fail gate on whether the parallel sub-line appears, but a crash, error, or wrong row count would be a red-team finding

harness_bugs_found_and_fixed: redteam_adversarial.py RT-10/RT-11 initially hashed raw csql multi-statement output including the per-statement '=== <Result of SELECT Command in Line N> ===' header, whose line number N varies by script position -- this produced spurious 'FAILED' results on the FIRST run of both RT-10 (10 distinct hashes) and a boundary-condition variant (2 distinct hashes from a trailing-whitespace asymmetry on the last block). Root-caused by direct inspection of the raw csql output, fixed in canon_block() (strip the header + rstrip trailing whitespace before hashing), then both variants re-run clean. This was a test-harness artifact, not an engine correctness issue -- recorded here for transparency, not hidden.
summary.product_source_correctness_findings: none -- no cross-variant (base vs IMP-015) result divergence found across the D6 TC re-run or any of the 9 adversarial battery cases (RT-01..RT-09), across 10x same-session repeats or 4-session concurrency stress on either variant, or on the real campaign DB's Q10/Q18
summary.mechanism_verification: D2(a) (caller-side HS_REJECT_ALL formula) confirmed firing correctly on 2 adversarial cases the D6 TC does not cover (NULL-mixed keys RT-05, composite keys RT-06), and confirmed NOT firing on a negative control it also does not cover (extreme low selectivity RT-08); D4 (order-sensitive aggregates unaffected) confirmed on a differently-shaped table (RT-09) with the group-by fallback sort itself parallel on both variants, identically; both target queries Q10/Q18 confirmed exhibiting the predicted parallel-workers trace sub-line on the real campaign database with the actual patched binary
